description_full: Jinko Holdings Limited, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the design, development, production, and marketing of photovoltaic products. The company provides solar modules, silicon wafers, solar cells, recovered silicon materials, and silicon ingots. It offers solar system integration services; solar power generation and solar system EPC services; and energy storage system, as well as undertakes solar power projects. The company sells its products to distributors, project developers, system integrators, and manufacturers of solar power products under the JinkoSolar brand. As of December 31, 2025, it had an integrated annual capacity of 120 gigawatts (GW) for mono wafers; 95 GW for solar cells; and 130 GW for solar modules. It operates in China, the United States, India, Saudi Arabia, Australia, Pakistan, Brazil, Poland, Japan, Spain, and Germany. Jinko Holdings Limited was formerly known as JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Jinko Holdings Limited in October 2026. The company was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Guangxin, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: Jinko Holdings Limited is a small-cap technology business with a $492M market cap on $9.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $316M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, thin -6.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 16.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 44% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
